paper.title: PAUSE: Low-Latency and Privacy-Aware Active User Selection for Federated Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Privacy-aware active user selection for FL (CMAB with latency, generalization and privacy reward)
unmapped: Reward of a set is min over selected users of tau_min/tau_{k,t} (non-linear, bottleneck) plus bounded history-dependent generalization and privacy terms Phi_g, Phi_p that depend on past selection counts
Regret is measured against a history-dependent Genie policy knowing the expected latency ratios mu_k
The learner knows the minimal latency tau_min
Users' expected latencies are pairwise distinct with minimal difference delta > 0
settings.definition_quote: We model this delay via the random variable $\tau_{t,k}$ ... drawn in an i.i.d. manner from a device specific distribution ... We denote the minimal difference between these terms as $\delta \triangleq \min_{i\neq j \in \bK}  |\E[\tau_i] - \E[\tau_j]|$ ... $r(\cS, t) \triangleq \frac{\tau_{\min}}{\max_{k \in \cS} \tau_{k,t}} +  \alpha\cdot \Phi_{\rm g}(\cdot) + \gamma \cdot \Phi_{\rm p}(\cdot)$

symbols.Delta_rmax: maximal per-round reward gap between the Genie and any policy, bounded by max mu_k - min mu_k + alpha*range(Phi_g) + gamma*range(Phi_p) (Lemma 1)
symbols.delta_lat: minimal difference between users' expected latencies, min_{i != j} |E[tau_i] - E[tau_j]| > 0

conditions: latencies tau_{t,k} i.i.d. per user with tau_{t,k} >= tau_min > 0 a.s.
users have pairwise distinct expected latencies (delta > 0)
Phi_g and Phi_p are bounded functions
tuning: UCB exploration bonus sqrt((m+1) log t / T_k(t))

source.label: THMREGRET
source.quote: The regret of \ac{pause} holds \begin{equation} R^{\cP}(n) \leq K(\Delta_{\max} \!+\! \delta) \left(\frac{4(m\!+\! 1)\log(n)}{\delta^2} \!+\! 1\! +\! \frac{2\pi^2}{3}\right), \end{equation}

results.notes: Regret defined as E[sum_t r(G_t,t) - r(S_t,t)] against a history-dependent Genie policy (greedy per round with known means), hence quantity 'other' and comparator best_policy. Appendix proof ends with 4pi^2/3 instead of 2pi^2/3; theorem statement recorded. The proof uses an 'enhanced Genie' argument. Brute-force policy computation is exponential in general (O(K log K) in the averaged special case via Pivot-and-Fill).
